DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE | Clearing operations in full swing to help combat severe flooding across Metro Manila ✅

Amid the rain, personnel from the MMDA continue their clearing operations along major roads in Metro Manila to prevent further flooding.

MMDA Chair Atty. Don Artes called on the cooperation of the residents to avoid throwing their garbage in canals and waterways to prevent severe flooding and compromise the efficiency of the pumping stations.

Aside from the regular clearing operations, MMDA rescue personnel are also on standby along with the agency’s assets to provide immediate response.

The Quezon City Government is providing urgent assistance—including safe and affordable housing—to families affected by a landslide that struck Don Vicente, Sitio Veterans, Barangay Bagong Silangan on the morning of July 23.

Triggered by days of heavy and continuous rainfall, the incident caused a portion of land to erode, displacing three families and damaging two vehicles. The affected area has long been classified as a non-buildable zone due to geohazards, and residents had previously been advised by both the barangay and city government to relocate. The site is also privately owned by a subdivision, making the construction of retaining structures unfeasible.

data.text:
Why take out loans of over $800 million to develop an airport where 95% of arrivals end up heading to other islands or resorts across the Maldives either by sea or seaplane?

If the airport had been leased, we wouldn’t be giving up an ounce of our sovereignty, despite what many loudly claim. Instead, we’d gain the funds needed to develop major international airports in key regions across the country. This would make travel easier for both tourists and locals and would likely double visitor numbers by lowering travel costs.

Many international airports around the world are either developed or operated by companies from outside the host country. For example, GMR operated Delhi and Hyderabad airports in India and currently operates Mactan-Cebu International Airport in the Philippines. Similarly, Changi Airports International from Singapore manages airports in Brazil and the Middle East. These are globally respected operators, bringing in expertise, investment, and efficiency without compromising national sovereignty.

This isn’t just about tourism. It would directly contribute to regional development and create thousands of job opportunities for Maldivians.

We don’t need a hundred small airports scattered across the Maldives. What we need are a few strategically located, large international airports that can handle traffic efficiently and ease the pressure on Malé.

So why is it that Maldivian governments rarely think beyond Malé?

What real development has VIA brought to the Maldives after all these years under the government-owned SOE, MACL?

They couldn’t even fix a leaking roof that was flooding the departure terminal, so what exactly are they capable of?
